description: A vintage distortion: a shelving tone control into a diode clipping stage modelled as a wave digital filter, in the manner of a Klon Centaur or a Tube Screamer

params.text: Lifts or cuts everything below 600Hz by up to 9dB before the clipper, using a first-order shelving filter rather than the Baxandall circuit the maker's manual describes
Lifts or cuts everything above 600Hz by up to 9dB before the clipper, using a first-order shelving filter rather than the Baxandall circuit the maker's manual describes
Sets the level going into the clipping stage, 0dB at the left to 30dB at the right
Adds a steady offset of up to 2.5V before the clipper, which pushes the signal off centre and brings even harmonics into the distortion

outputs.text: The distorted audio, with everything below 30Hz filtered out

notes: the clipper runs at twice the sample rate when the module is added; the oversampling menu changes that.
menu: Oversampling: 1x, 2x, 4x, 8x, 16x — sets how many times the internal sample rate is raised before the nonlinearity is computed; higher settings reduce aliasing and cost more CPU
